accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 75, printed 61, lines 16-20: the domain statement and each named category are accounted separately. This is a family of value-domain definitions and canonical references, not an independently executable universal-set oracle.

Each type has a valid-value set. Source-level type, its parameter values, rank and physical representation are not interchangeable. Sampling initialized objects cannot prove that a processor's full domain equals the defined domain.
The document fixes the logical domain; 7.4.5 p1 (PDF 87) identifies true and false. Different logical representation methods do not introduce extra language-level truth values.

Integer value sets are processor dependent. 7.4.3.1 (PDF 80-81) imposes separate minimum range and representation provisions. No fixed word width, two's-complement encoding or full-domain executable is inferred here.

Character value sets are processor dependent. 7.4.4.1-.2 (PDF 84-85) supplies kind/length and character-set premises. Fortran source characters do not establish native ASCII, every nondefault repertoire, collating codes or external encodings.
Real value sets are processor dependent. 7.4.3.2 (PDF 81-82) supplies approximation methods and qualified inquiries, not a universal IEEE representation or exact decimal-to-binary model.

The complex domain consists of combinations of the real and imaginary part values; 7.4.3.3 p1-p2 (PDF 83) makes them an ordered pair sharing a real approximation method selected by the complex kind. This is neither two arbitrary independent kinds nor permission to use relational ordering on complex operands.

7.5.8 p1-p2 (PDF 106) defines sequences of component values. Pointer association is a component value; an allocatable component contributes allocation status and, only when allocated, its dynamic type, parameters, bounds and value. Do not read undefined payloads or treat all components as plain storage bytes.

7.6.1 p1-p3/p7 (PDF 109-110) supplies the enum domain, tied to the integer kind of interoperable enumerators and its representation. It is not limited to the listed enumerator values. The enum type has no type parameter; its enumerators are integer named constants.

7.6.2 p1/p3/p5 (PDF 111-112) lists the possible enumeration values and constrains constructors by their valid positive ordinal positions. These values are not the open integer-correspondence domain of an enum type.

review_rationale: Independent original-source review and verified gate repairs: doc/source_audits/batch_007.json. The scoped type classification is accounted for without allocating fake executable effects or losing canonical ownership.
